status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: Check Point reported that the channel was no longer available and that OpenAI confirmed decommissioning of the identified internal Artifactory instance. This demonstrates removal of the reported attack path. It does not establish universal prevention of other covert channels.

review.requirement_proposition: Only store sensitive data used during AI model development, including production data, within organization-approved environments and locations within those environments.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: PO.5.1 R2 (Only store sensitive data used during AI model development, including production data, within organization-approved environments and locations within those environments.) governs AI model development and handling its sensitive data/code. The demonstrated released-agent cross-account tool workflow is not an evidenced model-development operation; runtime prompt/task injection does not establish development-code execution.

review.reason_for_change: The occurrence concerns released ChatGPT sessions and connected Gmail data. No sensitive-data storage location in a model-development environment is identified.

review.requirement_proposition: Avoid unwarranted authority, communicate uncertainty and encourage authoritative-source consultation.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: Check Point’s June 2026 research documents a ChatGPT shared-Artifactory channel and covert transfer pathway in a task workflow. For IEEE-7014.1 6.25.3(a-c), the missing applicability fact is whether the operator adopted IEEE 7014.1 for an emulated-empathy GPAI partner in this interaction; authoritative task output, including professional-domain output, does not alone establish a personalised or emotionally affirming partnering context. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: The exploit concerns code-execution sessions and hidden cross-account tool instructions. No emulated-empathy partner interaction or unwarranted advisory authority is identified.

review.requirement_proposition: Provide human subjects with options to withdraw participation or revoke their consent for present or future use of their data in GAI applications.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: MS-2.2-003 concerns human-subject participation and present/future data-use consent. The technical proof of concept establishes cross-account execution, but not a governed participant research programme, voluntary Profile undertaking or withdrawal arrangement.

review.reason_for_change: The proof of concept does not identify a human-subject evaluation consent or withdrawal process. A victim-session role in a security test is a different object.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: The demonstrated shared-service channel enabled one account to covertly task another session and receive connected Gmail data. That cross-account security outcome is Not aligned. The source documents a proof of concept, not a known population of maliciously affected users.

review.requirement_proposition: Enforce governance constraints in a structural layer independent of model inference so model outputs cannot use an authorized pathway to override, bypass or modify the controls applied to their operations.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS-GV-05 materially concerns inference-independent runtime controls, but the sources establish no SDOS adoption or conformance context. The exploit alone neither creates this voluntary undertaking nor establishes its whole structural-control proposition.

review.reason_for_change: Check Point demonstrated hidden cross-account tasking through shared internal service state. Model-directed execution in the victim session relayed connected Gmail data to the other account. The intended isolation boundary did not constrain that authorised tool pathway. The result covers the demonstrated channel, not every ChatGPT session.

review.requirement_proposition: Encode inputs and outputs to prevent the execution of unauthorized code.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: PW.5.1 R3 (Encode inputs and outputs to prevent the execution of unauthorized code.) governs AI model development and handling its sensitive data/code. The demonstrated released-agent cross-account tool workflow is not an evidenced model-development operation; runtime prompt/task injection does not establish development-code execution.

review.reason_for_change: The demonstrated vector is covert instructions in shared service state. The source does not establish that unsafe character encoding caused inputs or outputs to execute as unauthorised program code. Deliberate tool commands are distinct from that encoding mechanism.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence demonstrates a trust-boundary and authority-propagation failure in which legitimate capabilities granted to one user's session could be exercised in response to attacker-controlled instructions delivered across an unintended cross-account communications path. The victim's authority to let ChatGPT access connected Gmail data did not imply authority for another account to task that session or receive the retrieved information. The material mechanism therefore combines tenant-isolation failure, hidden instruction execution and transposition of user-granted tool authority across an identity boundary. The observed hidden task and disclosure retain source-authority and changed-principal failures, bounded to the demonstrated pathway. Released agent tool use is distinct from model-development security; human research consent and an SDOS undertaking are not established. Decommissioning the component does not prove universal prevention.
conclusion_change.new: The occurrence demonstrates a trust-boundary and authority-propagation failure in which legitimate capabilities granted to one user's session could be exercised in response to attacker-controlled instructions delivered across an unintended cross-account communications path. The victim's authority to let ChatGPT access connected Gmail data did not imply authority for another account to task that session or receive the retrieved information. The material mechanism therefore combines tenant-isolation failure, hidden instruction execution and transposition of user-granted tool authority across an identity boundary. The observed hidden task and disclosure retain source-authority and changed-principal failures, bounded to the demonstrated pathway. Released agent tool use is distinct from model-development security; human-subject research consent is not the demonstrated workflow. Decommissioning the component does not prove universal prevention. The structural isolation and safe-functioning outcomes are Not aligned for the proof of concept. Removal of the identified channel is Aligned with the intervention requirement.
